A man holds up a sign reading "Smash Patriarchy" during a solidarity rally organised by Men Against Violence Against Women on Bundesplatz in Bern, Switzerland, on November 14, 2026 [Anthony Anex/EPA]By Al Jazeera Staff and The Associated PressPublished On 15 Nov 202615 Nov 2026
Hundreds of men have led a demonstration in Switzerland’s capital, Bern, to denounce misogyny and violence against women, saying men need to take a more effective role in fighting both.
The “Men Against Violence Against Women” rally outside parliament on Saturday follows persistent concerns that misogyny is too prevalent online among teenage boys and young men and that other men need to build a stronger counter-narrative.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3What European students can learn from their Serbian peerslist 2 of 3Why did Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resign, and who is Colette Kress?list 3 of 3Deadly ‘racist’ attack in France: Are hate crimes rising in Europe?end of list
The misogynistic views are pushed by the right-wing “manosphere” – a loose network of online forums and influencers that promote male supremacy and hostility to feminism. Such influencers were emboldened after Donald Trump won the US presidential election in 202 to justify and amplify misogynistic derision and threats online.
“We men are part of the problem – the problem being violence against women and queer people,” said Christoph Gosteli, a 42-year-old social worker who co-organised the rally with a group called maenner.

SpaceX's Starship upper-stage vessel descends towards the mechanical tower catch at Starbase, Texas, on November 14, 2026 [AFP]By AP and ReutersPublished On 15 Nov 202615 Nov 2026
SpaceX’s Starship ‌spacecraft has returned to Earth, caught midair by giant mechanical arms where its journey began 22 hours earlier.
The spaceship emerged from a cloudy sky on Saturday, descending slowly over Starbase before slipping smoothly between mechanical “chopstick arms” above Launch Pad 2 in Texas – the first-ever capture of a Starship flying back from space.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3Which countries have sent people to space?list 2 of 3Fiery end for SpaceX Starship missionlist 3 of 3SpaceX’s showpiece Starship rocket reaches orbit for first timeend of list
Soon afterwards, SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk congratulated his “incredible team”.
SpaceX officials said Saturday’s catch demonstrates Starship’s full reusability, crucial for rapid, low-cost recycling.
However, with the first-stage booster exploding shortly after Friday’s liftoff from Texas, the company fell short of its desired double catch.
Separating neatly from its booster before things went awry, the upper-stage spacecraft soared into orbit and released 26 advanced Starlink satellites.SpaceX Starship 42 returns from orbit to the launchpad on the 15th test flight from the SpaceX launch complex in Starbase, Texas, on November 14, 2026 [Steve Nesius/Reuters]
SpaceX’s Kate Tice said its engines stopped firing too soon on the way back down. The booster’s guidance system sensed it was not in the right position and automatically initiated the watery detour and self-destruction. Engineers are still investigating the cause.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, right, and his rival, Gadi Eisenkot, pose for a group photo after the swearing-in ceremony for Israeli lawmakers at the Knesset, Israel's parliament, in Jerusalem on November 10, 2026 [Ohad Zwigenberg/AP]By Al Jazeera StaffPublished On 14 Nov 202614 Nov 2026
Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has renewed his call for a national unity government with his rival, Gadi Eisenkot, saying only such a government can guarantee Israel’s security.
In a video statement on Saturday, Netanyahu said a meeting with Eisenkot on Thursday “only strengthened the conviction that it is essential to form a national unity government”.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3Netanyahu fights to stay relevant as Israel’s opposition closes inlist 2 of 3‘Greater Israel’: Christian Zionism’s role in US policylist 3 of 3Iranophobia: Netanyahu’s bid to transform fear into political survivalend of list
The prime minister said such a government could “eliminate the Iranian threat once and for all”, claiming Tehran would “not hesitate to use nuclear weapons against us”.
“Let’s meet in one room, without preconditions,” he said.
Within minutes, however, Eisenkot dismissed the appeal as a ploy.
A former army chief, Eisenkot said Netanyahu “knows he lost the election”.
“Netanyahu is calling for negotiations while they are already underway,” he said. “These tricks don’t work on me.”
Who has the numbers?
Neither side won a majority in the October 27 election. Netanyahu’s right-wing and religious bloc took 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, Eisenkot’s four-party bloc got 48 seats, and Arab-led parties won a record 19.

Deadly car bomb blast kills two near Syria's capitalBy Al Jazeera StaffPublished On 14 Nov 202614 Nov 2026
A blast from a suspected explosive device planted inside a car in a suburb of the Syrian capital, Damascus, has killed at least two people, including a child, and wounded one.
The explosion in Jaramana, on the southeastern edge of Damascus, on Saturday killed a man and his daughter, while a third person, said to be the wife of the man, was seriously injured.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3Syria considering entry into Mecca defence pact, says foreign ministerlist 2 of 3External parties using Iraq to launch attacks on neighbours: Iraqi FMlist 3 of 3Deadly car bomb blast kills two near Syria’s capitalend of list
Syria’s Internal Security Forces said they sealed off the area and opened an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the blast.
Jaramana is home to a large community of the Druze religious minority and has seen tensions between some Druze members and the Sunni majority backing President Ahmed al-Sharaa’s government.
Witnesses described the vehicle as a Kia Rio parked between two apartment buildings in Jaramana, which is largely considered a quiet residential area, said Al Jazeera’s Heidi Pett, reporting from the blast scene.
Pett said the security situation in the capital remains complex, despite improvements since the regime of former President Bashar al-Assad fell two years ago.
“In the last couple of months, there were two very high-profile incidents,” she said, including a double-tap attack in July during French President Emmanuel Macron’s visit, which Syrian authorities attributed to a cell affiliated with ISIL (ISIS).

Denmark's Rasmus Hojlund scores his side's second goal [Luis Vieira/AP Photo]By AFPPublished On 14 Nov 202614 Nov 2026
Portugal have been hammered 1-4 by Denmark, an embarrassing Nations League defeat in their first match without Cristiano Ronaldo, following the superstar forward’s retirement from international football.
Rasmus Hojlund starred with a superb brace on Saturday as second place Denmark close in on a spot in the quarterfinals with a brilliant display in Braga.
The Danes are on nine points from five fixtures, three behind Portugal, who were already sure of qualification for the last eight having won all four of their previous group fixtures.
A draw against third-placed Norway on Tuesday, 3-1 winners over Wales earlier, will see Denmark through.
Ahead of kickoff, Portugal paid tribute to Ronaldo, who announced his exit from the international game last week, with the team and mascots walking out wearing Ronaldo’s number seven and his name on their jerseys.
Fans held up a huge banner that read “Thank you, captain” as the teams entered the field, while applause rolled around the stadium once the match clock hit seven.
Ronaldo made his debut for Portugal in 2003 and went on to establish world records for goals and appearances in international football, netting 146 times in 234 matches.
The highlight of his international career was winning Euro 2016, but it ended badly when the 41-year-old fell out with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus over not being selected for a Nations League fixture in September.
That row led to the five-time Ballon d’Or winner being handed a 30-day suspension by the Portuguese football federation and his subsequent retirement, and Portugal, in a dismal display, looked like they needed prime Ronaldo.
